TARGET 2.1: By 2030, end hunger and ensure access by all people, in particular the poor and people in vulnerable situations, including infants, to safe, nutritious and sufficient food all year round

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "", "transportation": "", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: medium_long_term

JUSTIFICATION:
The end-use of green hydrogen and its derivates as green ammonia has positive potential by promoting agricultural productivity and offering sustainability for food production. The efficient use of green ammonia-based fertilizers can optimize nutrient utilization and promote food security and sustainable agricultural practices.

TARGET 2.3: By 2030, double the agricultural productivity and incomes of small-scale food producers, in particular women, indigenous peoples, family farmers, pastoralists and fishers, including through secure and equal access to land, other productive resources and inputs, knowledge, financial services, markets and opportunities for value addition and non-farm employment

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: medium_long_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain has the positive potential to foster the local production of fertilizers by utilizing localized renewable energy resources, thereby reducing the reliance on imported fertilizers. Green hydrogen value chain and its derivates as green ammonia can promote agricultural productivity, reduce dependence on food and fertiliser imports, and implement sustainable local agriculture. To meet this target, the reciprocal interdependence between transportation and end-use can increase the agricultural productivity and incomes of small-scale food producers by 2030.

TARGET 2.4: By 2030, ensure sustainable food production systems and implement resilient agricultural practices that increase productivity and production, that help maintain ecosystems, that strengthen capacity for adaptation to climate change, extreme weather, drought, flooding and other disasters and that progressively improve land and soil quality

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "", "transportation": "", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: medium_long_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain and its derivates as green ammonia have positive potential by improving land and soil poverty and be used in producing carbon-neutral fertiliser products, decarbonising the food value chain. Green ammonia offers a sustainable alternative for nitrogen supply while emitting fewer greenhouse gases.

TARGET 3.9: By 2030, substantially reduce the number of deaths and illnesses from hazardous chemicals and air, water and soil pollution and contamination

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Adopting green hydrogen as a clean energy source may support efforts to reduce the adverse effects of pollution and contamination and may be the optimal strategy for air pollution mitigation, mainly replacing fossil fuels. In addition, green hydrogen has the positive potential to decarbonize multiple sectors reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Green hydrogen production can contribute to the replacement of fossil fuels and decrease pollution when the electricity used to produce green hydrogen comes from green methods. Green hydrogen transportation remains a challenge when fossil fuels are used as the fuel source for transporting green hydrogen, for example, in ships. However, green ammonia and green hydrogen may become the main fuel for zero carbon emissions of ships in the future. Green hydrogen end-use can reduce air pollution and avoid deaths and breathing illnesses, particularly in sectors such as transport. In some European countries, there are actions to decarbonize the transport sector by 2030, mainly to avoid local pollution. Meanwhile, in developing countries, replacing fossil fuels in this freight transportation is one of the main challenges foreseen in the medium-term.

TARGET 4.3: By 2030, ensure equal access for all women and men to affordable and quality technical, vocational and tertiary education, including university

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain has positive potential by investing in developing local research centres and educational institutions to build the hydrogen chain or parts of it, including partnerships between exporters and importers countries. The new opportunities for green hydrogen may lead to the development a novel educational proposal within the education system, which could offer equal access, such as "Women in Hydrogen."

TARGET 4.4: By 2030, substantially increase the number of youth and adults who have relevant skills, including technical and vocational skills, for employment, decent jobs and entrepreneurship

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain has positive potential by creating new and decent jobs and preparing skilled labour by implementing adequate education and training programmes and adopting far-sighted industrial and labour market policies. The demand for manpower in the green hydrogen value chain can play a vital role in enhancing educational training opportunities for both young people and adults.

TARGET 4.7: By 2030, ensure that all learners acquire the knowledge and skills needed to promote sustainable development, including, among others, through education for sustainable development and sustainable lifestyles, human rights, gender equality, promotion of a culture of peace and non-violence, global citizenship and appreciation of cultural diversity and of culture’s contribution to sustainable development

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain has positive potential by promoting research programmes in hydrogen technology and market, training programmes and partnerships between universities. These collaborative efforts should promote access to quality and free education mainly in developing countries.

TARGET 5.1: End all forms of discrimination against all women and girls everywhere

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "", "end_use": ""}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Despite the increasing number of work opportunities for women in the green hydrogen value chain, the production of green hydrogen in low-income countries, such as Africa, poses a significant risk (red flag) of widening the gender wage gap, and this concern can extend to other sectors/segments as well. As the green hydrogen value chain continues to expand and generate job opportunities, it is essential to remain mindful of potential gender disparities (red flag) in income and representation within the workforce.

TARGET 5.5: Ensure women’s full and effective participation and equal opportunities for leadership at all levels of decision-making in political, economic and public life

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "", "end_use": ""}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Despite the increasing number of work opportunities for women in the green hydrogen value chain, the production of green hydrogen in low-income countries, such as Africa, poses a significant risk (red flag) of widening the gender wage gap, and this concern can extend to other sectors/segments as well. As the green hydrogen value chain continues to expand and generate job opportunities, it is essential to remain mindful of potential gender disparities (red flag) in income and representation within the workforce.

TARGET 6.1: By 2030, achieve universal and equitable access to safe and affordable drinking water for all

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "", "end_use": ""}
VCA time horizon: medium_long_term

JUSTIFICATION:
In regions facing water stress or scarcity, it is crucial to explicitly consider the water source for green hydrogen production in strategies and provide detailed elaboration during project planning (red flag). The production of green hydrogen can also compete with the industrial and agriculture sectors by using water. In addition, it is necessary to ensure that the water demands for green hydrogen production do not compete with the existing demand for potable water, thus affecting water security.

TARGET 6.4: By 2030, substantially increase water-use efficiency across all sectors and ensure sustainable withdrawals and supply of freshwater to address water scarcity and substantially reduce the number of people suffering from water scarcity

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "direct_negative", "transportation": "", "end_use": ""}
VCA time horizon: medium_long_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Water usage is directed towards hydrogen production rather than allocated to consumption. Green hydrogen production in countries with water resource-scarce regions, such as Africa, must be cautiously approached due to the potential influence of water resource scarcity (red flag). The production of green hydrogen can also compete with the industrial and agriculture sectors by using water, affecting the end-use segment of the green hydrogen value chain. However, desalination techniques can be considered as an option in such cases.

TARGET 6.a: By 2030, expand international cooperation and capacity-building support to developing countries in water- and sanitation-related activities and programmes, including water harvesting, desalination, water efficiency, wastewater treatment, recycling and reuse technologies

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "direct_positive", "transportation": "", "end_use": ""}
VCA time horizon: medium_long_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen production by electrolysis can boost the use of new techniques and innovations, such as desalination. In certain cases where access to seawater is available, desalination can be utilized with minimal impact on cost and efficiency (green flag). For example, this opens up the possibility of deploying multi-purpose desalination facilities that can provide local benefits. Green hydrogen end-use can influence other sectors (e.g. industrial) by the use of this type of the technology.

TARGET 7.1: By 2030, ensure universal access to affordable, reliable and modern energy services

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "direct_positive", "end_use": "direct_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
As the description of the target, the green hydrogen value chain can positively potentialize access to affordable, reliable and modern energy services. Green hydrogen end-use can enhance direct access to affordable, reliable, and modern services. For example, it can replace fossil fuels in cooking and heating applications, facilitate the adoption of green hydrogen in the transport sector, and enable the development of decentralized off-grid energy solutions. Green hydrogen transportation can be used as energy storage, addressing the intermittency of renewable energy sources and ensuring a reliable and continuous energy supply. Green hydrogen production can promote the indirect deployment of renewable sources for energy generation in countries, such as Africa. To meet this target, the presence of the entire value chain at the local level can provide access to clean and sustainable energy sources.

TARGET 7.2: By 2030, increase substantially the share of renewable energy in the global energy mix

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "direct_positive", "transportation": "direct_positive", "end_use": "direct_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
The main source of producing green hydrogen is renewable energy, which can positively potentialize the increased share of renewable energy. Green hydrogen production and end-use can directly boost to increase the share of renewable energy in the global energy mix. Green hydrogen transportation can directly provide renewable energy storage. To meet this target, the presence of the entire value chain can facilitate the increase in local demand for renewable sources at the local level.

TARGET 7.3: By 2030, double the global rate of improvement in energy efficiency

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "direct_negative", "transportation": "indirect_negative", "end_use": "direct_negative"}
VCA time horizon: medium_long_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Higher energy efficiency in the green hydrogen value chain translates to better utilization of resources, development and improvement of technology, deployment of infrastructure and lower environmental impact that still needs to be achieved (red flag). Green hydrogen production and end-use still rely on technological advancements to improve the efficiency of the electrolysis process or hydrogen fuel cells. Green hydrogen transportation can indirectly enhance energy efficiency by effectively storing and utilizing renewable energy and balancing energy supply and demand since technology advances and cost becomes this possible.

TARGET 7.a: By 2030, enhance international cooperation to facilitate access to clean energy research and technology, including renewable energy, energy efficiency and advanced and cleaner fossil-fuel technology, and promote investment in energy infrastructure and clean energy technology

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "direct_positive", "transportation": "direct_positive", "end_use": "direct_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can positively direct contribute to the progress of the target based on its definition, providing mainly this international cooperation between developing and developed countries. Green hydrogen value chain can promote international cooperation to align with clean energy, investment in infrastructure and clean energy technology.

TARGET 7.b: By 2030, expand infrastructure and upgrade technology for supplying modern and sustainable energy services for all in developing countries, in particular least developed countries, small island developing States, and land-locked developing countries, in accordance with their respective programmes of support

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "direct_negative", "transportation": "direct_negative", "end_use": "direct_negative"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can direct contribute to the progress of the target based on its definition. Green hydrogen value chain can expand infrastructure and upgrade technology for supplying modern and sustainable energy services. Given that the production of green hydrogen for export is heavily concentrated in developing countries, it becomes essential to assess the potential for investments aimed at modernizing local infrastructure and services (red flag). To meet this target, the presence of the entire value chain can facilitate infrastructure expansion and technological advancement, crucial steps in ensuring access to clean energy for everyone by 2030.

TARGET 8.1: Sustain per capita economic growth in accordance with national circumstances and, in particular, at least 7 per cent gross domestic product growth per annum in the least developed countries

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain has the potential to positively influence per capita economic growth, taking into account the unique national circumstances and effectively balancing the supply and demand of electricity. For example, investing in domestic solution as green steel to export. To meet this target, the presence of the entire value chain can provide the creation of employment opportunities, attract investment, stimulate innovation, drive overall economic growth, and mitigate climate change impacts, and enhance energy security at the local level.

TARGET 8.2: Achieve higher levels of economic productivity through diversification, technological upgrading and innovation, including through a focus on high-value added and labour-intensive sectors

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "indirect_negative", "end_use": "indirect_negative"}
VCA time horizon: medium_long_term

JUSTIFICATION:
The concentration of patents in Europe and Japan, along with the reliance on labor export to low-income countries, can potentially pose challenges in the segments of the green hydrogen value chain (red flag). To meet this target, the presence of the entire value chain can enhance economic productivity through diversification, technological upgrading, innovation, and job creation at the local level.

TARGET 8.3: Promote development-oriented policies that support productive activities, decent job creation, entrepreneurship, creativity and innovation, and encourage the formalization and growth of micro-, small- and medium-sized enterprises, including through access to financial services

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can positively influence by creating new job opportunities including in other sectors, promoting sustainable economic growth, and developing and deploying green hydrogen technologies, which can stimulate innovation and entrepreneurship. To meet this target, the presence of the entire value chain can promote development-oriented policies that support productive activities, such as decent job creation and innovation.

TARGET 8.4: Improve progressively, through 2030, global resource efficiency in consumption and production and endeavour to decouple economic growth from environmental degradation, in accordance with the 10-year framework of programmes on sustainable consumption and production, with developed countries taking the lead

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen production and end-use can reduce the consumption of fossil fuels, contributing to resource efficiency and sustainable consumption and production patterns (green flag). To meet this target, production and end-use segments of the green hydrogen value chain can provide global resource efficiency and decouple economic growth from environmental degradation at the local level.

TARGET 8.5: By 2030, achieve full and productive employment and decent work for all women and men, including for young people and persons with disabilities, and equal pay for work of equal value

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "", "end_use": ""}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen production in low-income countries (e.g., Africa) represents a high risk of a gender wage gap (red flag). Once green hydrogen opens up a range of job opportunities, it is necessary to emphasize equal value in the workforce.

TARGET 8.7: Take immediate and effective measures to eradicate forced labour, end modern slavery and human trafficking and secure the prohibition and elimination of the worst forms of child labour, including recruitment and use of child soldiers, and by 2025 end child labour in all its forms

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "", "end_use": ""}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
The large-scale production of green hydrogen can allow developed countries to decarbonize their domestic economies while simultaneously exploiting the resources and labor (e.g., child labor and frequency of forced labor) of developing nations such as Africa (red flag).

TARGET 9.1: Develop quality, reliable, sustainable and resilient infrastructure, including regional and transborder infrastructure, to support economic development and human well-being, with a focus on affordable and equitable access for all

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_negative", "transportation": "direct_negative", "end_use": "indirect_negative"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
The infrastructure directly influence the local and cross-border production and end-use of green hydrogen, and green hydrogen transportation still requires a sustainable and robust infrastructure, with significant investments in pipelines, storage facilities, and transportation networks (red flag). The focus needs to be on affordable and equitable access for all. For example, given that the production of green hydrogen for export is heavily concentrated in developing countries, it becomes essential to assess the potential for investments aimed at modernizing local infrastructure and services. To meet this target, the interconnected between production and transportation, and transportation and end-use can contribute to building robust infrastructure that supports economic development and human well-being.

TARGET 9.2: Promote inclusive and sustainable industrialization and, by 2030, significantly raise industry’s share of employment and gross domestic product, in line with national circumstances, and double its share in least developed countries

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "direct_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen end-use can directly contribute to the decarbonization of harder-to-abate sectors (e.g., steel and cement), promoting sustainable industrialization (green flag). The industry. The green hydrogen production and transportation can indirectly contribute to boosting a sustainable industry, mainly in national circumstances (green flag). To meet this target, the reciprocal relationship between transporting and using green hydrogen plays a vital role in promoting inclusive and sustainable industrialization. By facilitating the adoption of green hydrogen technology in industrial processes, this relationship contributes to economic growth while minimizing environmental impact.

TARGET 9.3: Increase the access of small-scale industrial and other enterprises, in particular in developing countries, to financial services, including affordable credit, and their integration into value chains and markets

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "indirect_positive", "transportation": "indirect_positive", "end_use": "indirect_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can indirectly provide a more diversified trade and industrialization route by integrating different sectors (transport, maritime, and industrial sectors) (green flag). To meet this target, the presence of the entire value chain can facilitate increased access for small-scale industrial, particularly in developing countries, to financial services, including affordable credit. Additionally, it can support their integration into value chains and markets.

TARGET 9.4: By 2030, upgrade infrastructure and retrofit industries to make them sustainable, with increased resource-use efficiency and greater adoption of clean and environmentally sound technologies and industrial processes, with all countries taking action in accordance with their respective capabilities

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "direct_positive", "transportation": "direct_positive", "end_use": "direct_positive"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can directly promote the upgrading of infrastructure and retrofitting of industries to make them sustainable by enhancing resource-use efficiency and fostering the adoption of green methods and technologies in industrial processes (green flag). To meet this target, transportation and end-use segments of the green hydrogen value chain can upgrade infrastructure and retrofit industries to make them sustainable. This involves increasing resource-use efficiency and promoting the adoption of clean and environmentally sound technologies and industrial processes at the local level.

TARGET 9.5: Enhance scientific research, upgrade the technological capabilities of industrial sectors in all countries, in particular developing countries, including, by 2030, encouraging innovation and substantially increasing the number of research and development workers per 1 million people and public and private research and development spending

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "direct_negative", "transportation": "indirect_negative", "end_use": "direct_negative"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can be negatively influenced by technology transfer issues from Global North countries to Global South countries (e.g., patente). To meet this target, production and transportation and, transportation and end-use segments of the green hydrogen value chain can enhance scientific research and upgrade technological capabilities across industrial sectors worldwide, with a particular emphasis on developing countries.

TARGET 9.a: Facilitate sustainable and resilient infrastructure development in developing countries through enhanced financial, technological and technical support to African countries, least developed countries, landlocked developing countries and small island developing States

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "direct_negative", "transportation": "direct_negative", "end_use": "direct_negative"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can face negative influences, primarily in developing countries, due to its dependence on technology transfer, limited technical expertise, and financial barriers. Mainly transportation of green hydrogen, which presents the possibility of developed countries externalizing their carbon-intensive activities to developing nations in case of exportation and importation. To meet this target, production and transportation and, transportation and end-use segments of the green hydrogen value chain can aid in facilitating sustainable and resilient infrastructure development at the local level.

TARGET 9.b: Support domestic technology development, research and innovation in developing countries, including by ensuring a conducive policy environment for, inter alia, industrial diversification and value addition to commodities

VCA cells for this target (segment: influence): {"production": "direct_negative", "transportation": "indirect_negative", "end_use": "direct_negative"}
VCA time horizon: short_term

JUSTIFICATION:
Green hydrogen value chain can be negatively influenced by technology transfer issues from Global North countries to Global South countries and the concentration of patents in Europe and Japan.
